description: Cases of the identifiability checks: the Gram matrix of the covariance parameters, the degrees of freedom between levels, levels against the dimension of a random term and random effects confounded with the residual.

cases.description: A random intercept of a factor with three levels of two rows: the Gram matrix of the variance and the residual has full rank, so identified.

message.text: The design identifies every covariance parameter, the residual variance included (2 in all).

cases.description: One row per level: the projected bases of the intercept variance and the residual are proportional, so C has an eigenvalue 0, both parameters are confounded and the design does not identify them.

message.text: The design does not identify the covariance parameters of the random part: the Gram matrix of their bases has rank 1 for 2 parameters. Parameters that the fixed effects absorb: none. Parameters that cannot be separated from one another: '1 | g: var((Intercept))' and 'residual'.

cases.description: The grouping factor is also a fixed effect: the projection removes the basis of its intercept variance, which vanishes, and the residual alone remains in C, so not_identified with one vanishing parameter and none confounded.

cases.description: The family 'poisson' gives the class poisson: the unprojected basis without a residual has full rank, so necessary_condition_met.

cases.description: One row per subject and item: the intercept of 'subject:item' alone has no replicated cell, so confounded, whereas the intercepts of 'item' and 'subject' have replicated cells.

Combinations of a level of 'subject' and a cell of '1 | subject' that have two or more rows: 2 of 2.
Each combination of a level of 'subject:item' and a cell of '1 | subject:item' has one row, so the random effects of '1 | subject:item' are confounded with the residual and not identified.

cases.description: A correlated term of a factor with one row per subject and condition: confounded.

message.text: Each combination of a level of 'subject' and a cell of '1 + cond | subject' has one row, so the random effects of '1 + cond | subject' are confounded with the residual and not identified.

cases.description: Uncorrelated terms of a frozen factor with one row per subject and condition: each term's pattern covers both one-column terms of 'subject', no cell is replicated and neither is correlated or an intercept alone, so coding_dependent for both.

message.text: Each combination of a level of 'subject' and a cell of '1 | subject' and '0 + cond | subject' has one row. With uncorrelated random effects, '0 + cond | subject' is identified only through the restriction that the coding imposes, if at all, and the result changes with the coding. identifiability.gram_rank decides whether the coding chosen identifies it.

cases.description: z is constant within the levels of 'g' up to rounding: the first row of 'a' holds 0.30000000000000004, the double nearest to 0.1 + 0.2, and the other two the double nearest to 0.3, one bit apart. The column of z in X_d has the largest absolute value of about 5.6e-17, at most 1e-7 times 3.3, the largest absolute value of z, so it is set to 0 and rank(X_d) is 0, as the indicator columns of the levels would absorb it in the sequential rule: budget 4 - 2 + 0 = 2, with the intercept and z as consuming terms.

cases.description: A level whose slope the fixed effects absorb, with values 400 times those of the other level, hides nothing: the other level's column is orthogonal to X and gives a level ratio of 1, whereas M_kk divided by tr(A_k Z'Z A_k Z'Z) is about 1e-11, so the variance does not vanish and C, with the off-diagonal element 1/2, has the eigenvalues 1/2 and 3/2.

message.text: The design identifies every covariance parameter, the residual variance included (2 in all).

cases.description: A covariance whose basis cancels across the levels: with v = P z for the intercept column z of the level of three rows, the projected columns of the intercept are v and -v and those of the slope v and v, so that the parts of the covariance's basis, 2vv' and -2vv', cancel. Its level ratios are 1/16 and 9/16 and its cancellation ratio 0, so it vanishes, and the two variances, each with the basis 2vv', are confounded beside the residual.
